act.description: Act is the plugin action, written plugin/action.

with.description:
With gives the action's arguments. Values are literal unless the whole
value is "${ expr }".

confirm.description:
Confirm is the question asked to the user before an irreversible
action. The action runs only after a clear yes.

idempotencyKey.description:
IdempotencyKey is a string expression identifying the effect, so it is
not repeated. Required for irreversible actions.

milestone.description: Milestone is recorded when the effect is confirmed.

Action.description: Action is a call to a plugin action with an effect on the world.

text.description: Text is the question sent to the user.

choices.description:
Choices is an expression producing the list the user picks from. When
set, the reply is matched to one element; otherwise it is extracted as
the input's type.

minConfidence.description:
MinConfidence is the lowest confidence at which the interpretation is
accepted, between 0 and 1. Every decision declares one.

onLowConfidence.description:
OnLowConfidence says what happens below minConfidence. Every decision
declares it.

Ask.description:
Ask asks the user for a value and interprets the reply with the Decide
engine.

instructions.description: Instructions say what to decide from the shared state.

choice.description: Choice maps option keys to descriptions.

score.description: Score lists ordered levels, lowest first.

BatchQuestion.description: BatchQuestion asks exactly one choice, yesNo or score question.

else.description: Else marks the last case, taken when no other matched.

call.description: Call runs another Function; with gives its inputs.

with.description: With gives the arguments of call.

escalate.description: Escalate hands over to a person.

BranchCase.description:
BranchCase is one case of a branch. Exactly one of when and else must be
set, and exactly one of call, respond and escalate.

Compensate.description: Compensate has no settings; each action's compensation comes from its plugin.

cel.description: CEL is an expression; its value is the step's output.

starlark.description: Starlark calls a function of a script file.

Compute.description:
Compute is a deterministic computation. Exactly one of cel and starlark
must be set.

state.description: State is shared by every question and masked before leaving the process.

questions.description: Questions names independent questions; they cannot read each other's answers.

minConfidence.description: MinConfidence is the minimum winning probability for each answer.

onLowConfidence.description:
OnLowConfidence is fail (run onError) or continue (null only uncertain answers).
Provider errors or missing answers always run onError, even with continue.

DecideBatchStep.description:
DecideBatchStep groups independent questions without changing their dependencies.
Later steps read output.answers.<name>.value and probability. A low-confidence
answer has value null when onLowConfidence is continue. output.value is the map
of values only when every question meets the threshold; otherwise it is null.
Never treat a null answer as permission or as an absent user restriction.

state.description:
State is what the question is about. It is masked for personal data
before it leaves the process.

choice.description: Choice maps each option key to its description.

score.description: Score lists ordered levels, lowest first.

minConfidence.description: MinConfidence is the lowest probability of the answer that is acted on.

onLowConfidence.description:
OnLowConfidence says what happens below minConfidence: human asks a
person (an answer task with the options), fail fails the step, and
continue sets output.value to null so a later branch can handle it.

DecideStep.description:
DecideStep asks the Decide engine one question about a state. Exactly one
of choice, yesNo and score must be set. The step's output is
{value, probability, probabilities}: value is the chosen key (choice),
true or false (yesNo), or the most probable level (score).

when.description:
When is a boolean expression: the strategy runs only when it is
true. It reads the failure as sources.error (code, message, definite)
besides inputs, steps and caller, e.g. "sources.error.code ==
'CONFLICT'". It only narrows the chain: an irreversible action whose
outcome is unknown is still verified first and never repeated or
re-routed blind (#30).

probe.description:
Probe asks the external system whether the failed effect happened
anyway. The action's plugin must declare verify mode probe or native.

retry.description:
Retry tries again. After an irreversible action it is allowed only
when the plugin verifies natively or a probe proved nothing happened.

fallback.description:
Fallback takes another path: another function, another action, or a
fixed value.

escalate.description: Escalate creates a human task and waits for it.

compensate.description: Compensate undoes earlier effects of the same run, in reverse order.

respond.description: Respond sends a message to the user and ends the run.

fail.description: Fail ends the run as failed.

ErrorStrategy.description: ErrorStrategy is one step of an onError chain. Exactly one field must be set.

queue.description: Queue is the HumanQueue that receives the task.

task.description: Task is the kind of human task.

message.description: Message tells the human what is needed.

whileWaiting.description: WhileWaiting is sent to the user while the human task is open.

onDeny.description:
OnDeny is what the user hears when a person denies an approval
(task: approve); default: the Agent's messages.denied. A denied (or
unclear) approval ends the Function: no later step or action runs.

route.description:
Route sends the task to another queue by a declared rule: the first
rule whose when holds decides, else queue ("a discount above 50% goes
to the owner"). A rule, never a model's choice (RFC-0006).

when.description: When is a bool expression over inputs, steps and caller.

queue.description: Queue receives the task when it holds.

instructions.description:
Instructions add to the input's description, e.g. how to resolve
relative dates or which default not to assume.

future.description:
Future moves a date the model read as more than a week past to the
same day a year later: "10 de julho" said in September is next July.
Models often got the year wrong (agency-002); "ontem" stays past.

conversation.description:
Conversation lets the value come from what the user said earlier in
the conversation when the message leaves it out ("eu e minha esposa"
said before asking for a hotel). The message always wins. Leave it off
for values that belong to one request only, such as a new trip's
dates (agency-002).

Extract.description: Extract reads an input from the conversation.

message.description: Message is recorded with the failure.

Fail.description: Fail ends the run as failed.

act.description: Act is another plugin action to call instead, written plugin/action.

with.description:
With gives the arguments of function or act. Values are literal unless
the whole value is "${ expr }".

idempotencyKey.description: IdempotencyKey is required when act is irreversible.

useNull.description: UseNull continues without the value; the input becomes null.

Fallback.description:
Fallback settings. Exactly one of function, act and useNull must be set.
A fallback action is held to the same effect rules as the main action:
inside an input's onUnresolved it must be read-only, and when it is
irreversible it needs its own idempotencyKey.

spec.description: Spec is what the author wants the function to do.

Function.description:
Function is one capability of an agent: the inputs it needs, who may run
it, what must be true before it acts, the action it takes and what it
tells the user.

description.description:
Description says in one sentence what the function does. It is shown
to people and used by the router.

selector.description:
Selector says which events can start this function. A function
without a selector can only be called by other functions.

authorize.description:
Authorize is a boolean expression on caller (and inputs) that must be
true for the function to run. It is checked with the verified identity
of the caller, never with anything a model decided.

inputs.description:
Inputs the function needs, by name. Each is resolved from its sources
in order until one produces a value.

preconditions.description:
Preconditions must all be true, after inputs are resolved, before the
action runs.

steps.description:
Steps run in order after the preconditions and before the action.
Each step's result is readable by later steps, the action and the
output as steps.<id>.status and steps.<id>.output.

action.description: Action is the effect the function has on the world.

output.description: Output is what the user is told when the function succeeds.

onError.description:
OnError is the chain of strategies tried, in order, when the function
fails. Each item runs only if the previous one failed.

state.description:
State is the input. It is masked for personal data before it leaves
the process.

schema.description: Schema is a JSON Schema the output must match. Required for extract.

GenerateStep.description:
GenerateStep asks the Generate engine for text or an object. The reply is
validated against the schema locally, repaired once if needed, and
refused otherwise; the model is never trusted to follow the schema.

type.description:
Type of the value: a basic type (string, int, float, bool, date,
timestamp, duration, map, any), a type published by a plugin
(agenda.Slot), or list<T> of either. A date is a "YYYY-MM-DD"
string.

description.description:
Description says what the value is. Extraction and free-text
questions show it to the model, so write it for a reader: "the city
the user flies from".

resolve.description:
Resolve lists where the value can come from, tried in order. A source
may read the outputs of earlier sources of the same input as
sources.<id>.output.

onUnresolved.description: OnUnresolved runs when no source produced a value.

format.description:
Format marks personal data of a known shape: email, phone or cpf.
Its extract source and its free-text question read it from the
user's own words by pattern, in code: no model sees it, since models
only get masked text, where it is a placeholder (agency-001). The
type must be string.

Input.description: Input is one value the function needs.

name.description: Name of the milestone, e.g. agendou.

subject.description: Subject is the Subject kind, in the same namespace.

id.description: ID overrides the Subject's id expression here.

attributes.description: Attributes are expressions for the Subject's declared attributes.

MilestoneRef.description:
MilestoneRef records a business milestone when the step or the action
it is on succeeds. For an effect that means confirmed: a cancelled or
unverified effect records nothing. It is recorded once, however often
the run is resumed.

name.description:
Name of the resource, unique per kind within its namespace. Lowercase
letters, digits and hyphens, starting and ending with a letter or digit.

namespace.description: Namespace the resource belongs to, usually one per customer.

labels.description: Labels are free-form key/value pairs for selecting and grouping.

template.description:
Template is the message sent to the user; a function called by
another sends nothing.

value.description:
Value is what a caller receives (call, fromFunction); by default the
action's output, or the rendered template.

guardrails.description: Guardrails checked before the message is sent, by name.

Output.description:
Output is what the function produces on success. At least one of
template and value must be set.

cel.description: CEL is the boolean expression that must be true.

message.description:
Message tells the user why the function cannot proceed. It is a
template: naming what was understood ("Entendi a ida como
{{ inputs.departDate }}") lets the user correct a misreading instead of
hearing it as a fact (agency-002).

Precondition.description: Precondition is a condition checked before the action.

Probe.description: Probe has no settings; the verification action comes from the plugin.

to.description:
To is "user" (the default) or "queue:<name>": a note to a human
queue that asks nothing and waits for nothing (a report, an alert).

bases.description: Bases are KnowledgeBase names of this namespace.

query.description:
Query is a string expression: what to search for, e.g.
"event.message".

k.description: K is how many passages at most, 1 to 10; default 4.

attempts.description: Attempts is the number of extra attempts.

backoff.description: Backoff is the wait before the first retry, as a duration like 2s.

intent.description: Intent is the name of the Intent this function handles.

description.description:
Description is what the router reads to choose this function; the
function's own description when empty. Write it in the users'
language, the way they ask for it: measured with Jev, a Portuguese
routing text moved "quero viajar" from 0.09 to 0.91
(docs/research/router-001.md).

after.description:
After makes this a follow-up: it is routable only when the
conversation's last run was one of these Functions ("e o da LATAM?"
only means something after a flight search). Measured: wording alone
did not stop general questions from reaching follow-ups
(docs/research/router-002.md).

who.description:
Who is a bool expression over caller: the router offers this
Function only to callers it matches, so a patient is never offered
a team Function (RFC-0006). authorize still decides.

Selector.description: Selector matches events to a function.

id.description: ID names the source so later sources can read its output.

when.description: When is a boolean expression; the source is skipped when it is false.

fromAction.description:
FromAction calls a plugin action, written plugin/action. Its effect
class must be read.

fromFunction.description: FromFunction calls another Function in the same namespace.

with.description:
With gives the arguments of fromAction or fromFunction. Values are
literal unless the whole value is "${ expr }".

value.description: Value computes the input directly with an expression.

extract.description:
Extract takes the value from the user's message with the Generate
engine; null when the message does not say. All extract sources of a
Function are answered by one model call.

ask.description: Ask asks the user and waits for the answer.

Source.description:
Source is one way to get an input's value. Exactly one of fromAction,
fromFunction, value, extract and ask must be set.

script.description:
Script is the path of the .star file, relative to the file that
declares the Function.

function.description: Function is the name of a top-level function of the script.

with.description:
With gives the function's keyword arguments. Values are literal unless
the whole value is "${ expr }".

StarlarkCall.description: StarlarkCall calls a top-level function of a Starlark script.

id.description: ID names the step; later steps read its result as steps.<id>.

when.description:
When is a boolean expression; the step is skipped when it is false,
and its status is then "skipped".

compute.description: Compute runs a CEL expression or a Starlark function.

act.description:
Act calls a plugin action, written plugin/action, with the guarantees
of its effect class.

call.description:
Call runs another Function of the same namespace; with gives its
inputs.

with.description:
With gives the arguments of act or call. Values are literal unless
the whole value is "${ expr }".

idempotencyKey.description:
IdempotencyKey is a string expression; required when act is
irreversible.

confirm.description:
Confirm is asked before an act step runs; the step runs only on a
clear yes.

decideBatch.description: DecideBatch asks independent named questions about one shared state in one request.

extract.description:
Extract fills a JSON Schema from a state with the Generate engine; the
output is the validated object.

generate.description: Generate writes text, or an object when a schema is given.

ask.description: Ask asks the user to choose from a list and waits for the answer.

respond.description: Respond sends a message to the user and continues.

escalate.description:
Escalate creates a HumanTask and waits; the person's answer is the
step's output.

branch.description:
Branch runs the first case whose condition is true. It must end with
an else case, so every situation is covered.

experiment.description:
Experiment assigns the subject a variant of an Experiment, records
that the subject saw it, and outputs the variant's name; later steps
branch on it. The same subject always gets the same variant.

wait.description:
Wait sleeps durably: the run waits for a time, not for a message, and
survives restarts. Its output is the time it woke.

retrieve.description:
Retrieve searches the namespace's KnowledgeBases (retrieve-001). Its
output is the list of passages found, {source, section, text}, as
the free mode finds them: only bases the caller's audience may read,
no expired or suspended lesson, only passages relevant to the query.
Recorded, so a resumed run replays the same passages.

milestone.description:
Milestone is recorded when the step succeeds (for act: when the
effect is confirmed).

onError.description: OnError is tried, in order, when the step fails.

Step.description:
Step is one step of a Function (RFC-0001, "Tipos de passo"). Exactly one
of compute, act, call, decide, decideBatch, extract, generate, ask, respond, escalate,
branch and wait must be set. parallel, foreach, emit, remember and
delegate come later.

for.description:
For is a duration from when the step is first reached, in Go syntax
(90m, 36h). Days are business decisions; write them with until.

until.description:
Until is a timestamp expression, e.g. the next business day at 10h:
"atTime(addBusinessDays(event.time, 1, 'America/Sao_Paulo'), '10:00', 'America/Sao_Paulo')".

orReply.description:
OrReply ends the wait early when the user replies: while it waits
the run is the conversation's active run, so the reply comes here,
not to the router. The output is then {reply, timedOut}: the reply's
text and false, or null and true when the time came first.

includeSideMessages.description:
IncludeSideMessages opts this reply wait into preference capture. The host
uses a Jev batch to distinguish current factual questions and withdrawal;
answered side user messages are journaled without resuming the wait.
Requires orReply. Output.sideMessages is chronological, scoped to this
wait and caller, limited to 8 messages/32 KiB (overflow is an error).
Combine it explicitly with the current reply for preference extraction.
This context is never confirmation or permission to perform an effect.

relay.description:
Relay makes every reply this wait's own, as written: no side-question
classification. For a wait that relays a conversation with a person
("Confirma que quer remarcar?"), where a question back is for that
person, not for the free mode (agency-003). Requires orReply.

events.description:
Events end the wait early when another system reports one of them
for this run's key: a Trigger with event (e.g. the CRM says the
lead's meeting was booked). The output is then {reply: null,
timedOut: false, event: <name>, payload: <the event's payload>};
with events, the output always has that shape.

Wait.description: Wait is a durable timer. Exactly one of for and until must be set.

name.description: Name of the event, as a Trigger's event.name delivers it.

key.description:
Key is a string expression identifying whom it is about, evaluated
when the wait starts (e.g. event.payload.leadId): only an event with
the same key ends this wait.

WaitEvent.description: WaitEvent is an event a wait listens for.
